PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Obedience means doing what you are told to do, gladly and in the right way. In this sub-strand you will read Exodus 20:12 and learn the benefit of honouring parents, see why we obey parents, teachers and school rules, and learn the results of disobedience so that you choose to obey in your daily life.

## Strand 4.0: Christian Values
Sub-strand 4.3: Obedience
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) read Exodus 20:12 and state the benefit of honouring parents
b) obey parents and teachers to promote harmonious co- existence
c) practise responsibility by obeying school rules
d) outline the results of disobedience
e) desire to exercise obedience in day-to-day life

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why is it important to obey?

## Core competencies
• Learning to learn: the skill of carrying out activities with peers is portrayed as learners list the results of disobedience.
• Creativity and Imagination: the skill of coming up with new ideas is nurtured as learners compose a poem on the benefits of obeying parents and teachers.

## Values
• Responsibility: learners obey parents and teachers.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Peace Education: learners contribute to peace at home by obeying their parents.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners recite poems.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing a song on the benefits of obedience.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 4.0 Christian Values, Sub-strand 4.3 Obedience
• Exodus 20:12; Ephesians 6:1-2; Genesis 3 (Good News Bible)
• KICD Grade 4 CRE radio programme 15 (Obedience at home)

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Honouring parents: Exodus 20:12

LESSON 1: HONOURING PARENTS: EXODUS 20:12
=========================================

## What you will learn
• Read Exodus 20:12 and state the benefit of honouring parents.
• Give ways of obeying and respecting parents and guardians at home.

Curriculum outcomes: a) read Exodus 20:12 and state the benefit of honouring parents; b) obey parents and teachers to promote harmonious co- existence

## Introduction
Your mother asks you to fetch water before you go out to play. You can grumble, delay, or go at once with a smile. Which one shows honour to your parent?

## Notes
### What is obedience?
Obedience means doing what you are told to do gladly and following instructions from those in authority over you. When we obey our parents and guardians, we show them respect.

### Exodus 20:12
God gave the Ten Commandments to Moses at Mount Sinai. The fifth commandment says (Good News Bible):

"Respect your father and your mother, so that you may live a long time in the land that I am giving you."

Other Bibles say "Honour your father and your mother." To honour means to respect, obey and value someone.

### The benefit of honouring parents
This commandment comes with a promise: those who honour their parents will live a long time in the land God gives them. Honouring parents also brings God's blessing, peace in the home and a good name. Paul repeats this commandment for children in Ephesians 6:1-2 and points out that it is the first commandment with a promise.

### Ways of honouring and obeying parents
- Doing chores when asked, such as sweeping, washing utensils or feeding animals.
- Speaking politely and not answering back rudely.
- Coming home on time and telling them where you are going.
- Taking their advice and correction without sulking.
- Greeting them and thanking them.
- Helping them when they are sick or tired.
- Praying for them.

### Obedience brings harmony at home
When children obey, parents are happy, there are fewer quarrels, and work is done quickly. Everyone lives together in peace. This is called harmonious co-existence.

If you live with a guardian, such as a grandmother, aunt or uncle, the same commandment applies: respect and obey the adults who care for you.

## Key words
• obedience — doing what you are told gladly and following instructions
• honour — to respect, obey and value someone
• harmonious co-existence — living together peacefully

## Activity: Reading Exodus 20:12 and composing a poem
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Read Exodus 20:12 together and state the benefit of honouring parents.
2. In groups, list things you do at home to obey your parents or guardians.
3. Compose a short poem on the benefits of obeying parents.
4. Recite your poem to the class.

## Practice
1. Recite Exodus 20:12.
2. What benefit does God promise to those who honour their parents?
3. Give three ways of honouring parents at home.

## Summary
• Exodus 20:12 commands us to respect our father and mother.
• The promise: a long life in the land God gives.
• Obedience brings peace at home.

### Answers to practice
1. Respect your father and your mother, so that you may live a long time in the land that I am giving you.
2. They will live a long time in the land God gives them.
3. Any three: doing chores when asked; speaking politely; coming home on time; accepting correction; greeting and thanking them; helping them; praying for them.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Obeying teachers and school rules

LESSON 2: OBEYING TEACHERS AND SCHOOL RULES
===========================================

## What you will learn
• Explain the importance of obeying teachers.
• State why school rules should be obeyed.
• Name school rules and how to keep them.

Curriculum outcomes: b) obey parents and teachers to promote harmonious co- existence; c) practise responsibility by obeying school rules

## Introduction
Imagine a school where nobody rings the bell on time, learners come and go as they wish, and no one listens to the teachers. Would anyone learn? Rules and obedience keep a school running well.

## Notes
### Why obey teachers?
Teachers take care of learners at school the way parents do at home. They teach, guide and protect us. When we obey teachers:
- we learn well and do our work on time;
- the class is calm and orderly;
- we are kept safe, for example when teachers warn us not to play near a road or a deep hole;
- we show respect, which pleases God.

### School rules
Every school has rules that everyone must follow. Common school rules include:
- Arrive at school on time.
- Wear the correct school uniform neatly.
- Respect teachers, workers and other learners.
- Do not fight, bully or use bad language.
- Keep the compound and classrooms clean.
- Take care of school property such as desks, books and water taps.
- Do not leave the school compound without permission.

### Why should we obey school rules?
- Rules keep order, so everyone can learn.
- Rules protect our safety and health.
- Rules teach us responsibility and self-discipline.
- Rules help us live in peace with others.
- Obeying rules prepares us to obey the laws of our country when we grow up.

### Obedience and responsibility
A responsible learner keeps the rules even when no teacher is watching. For example, he or she puts litter in the bin, closes a running tap, and lines up at the canteen without pushing.

Obeying parents, teachers and school rules helps us live well with others at home and at school. The Bible teaches Christians to obey those in authority because God is pleased when there is order and peace.

## Key words
• rule — an instruction that tells people what they must or must not do
• responsibility — doing your duty well without being forced
• self-discipline — controlling yourself to do what is right

## Activity: Our school rules
You will need: Manila paper, Markers
1. In groups, discuss the importance of obeying teachers.
2. List five rules of your school and say why each one should be obeyed.
3. Make a chart of 'Why we obey school rules' and display it in class.

## Practice
1. Give two reasons why learners should obey teachers.
2. Name three school rules.
3. Why should you keep school rules even when no teacher is watching?

## Summary
• Teachers guide and protect us, so we obey them.
• School rules keep order, safety and peace.
• A responsible learner obeys rules even when no one is watching.

### Answers to practice
1. Any two: to learn well; to keep order; to be safe; to show respect that pleases God.
2. Any three, for example arrive on time, wear correct uniform, do not fight, keep the compound clean, care for school property, do not leave school without permission.
3. Because a responsible learner does right always; God sees everything; rules protect everyone.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Results of disobedience

LESSON 3: RESULTS OF DISOBEDIENCE
=================================

## What you will learn
• Outline the results of disobedience.
• Show a desire to obey in day-to-day life.

Curriculum outcomes: d) outline the results of disobedience; e) desire to exercise obedience in day-to-day life

## Introduction
A boy is told not to swim in the river during the rains, but he goes anyway. A girl is told to finish her homework before watching television, but she refuses. Disobedience always has results.

## Notes
### What is disobedience?
Disobedience is refusing to do what we are told by God, parents, teachers or other people in authority, or doing what we have been told not to do.

### Disobedience in the Bible
In Genesis 3, God told Adam and Eve not to eat the fruit of the tree in the middle of the Garden of Eden. They disobeyed. As a result they felt ashamed, hid from God, and were sent out of the garden. Disobedience broke their close friendship with God.

### Results of disobedience
- Danger and injury: a child who plays near a busy road against instructions may be knocked by a vehicle.
- Punishment: a learner who breaks school rules may be punished.
- Poor performance: a learner who ignores the teacher's instructions may fail.
- Loss of trust: parents and teachers stop trusting a disobedient child.
- Quarrels and lack of peace at home and in school.
- Sadness and guilt.
- Sin: disobeying God and our parents does not please God.

### Results of obedience
- God's blessing and a long life (Exodus 20:12).
- Safety and good health.
- Trust, love and peace with others.
- Success in school work.

### Choosing to obey every day
Obedience is a daily choice. You can:
- listen carefully to instructions;
- obey quickly and cheerfully, without grumbling;
- ask politely when you do not understand an instruction;
- ask God to help you obey.

If an adult ever tells you to do something wrong, such as stealing, hiding a secret touch or going with a stranger, you should not obey. Say No and tell a trusted adult. Obeying God comes first.

## Key words
• disobedience — refusing to do what you are told by those in authority
• consequence — a result of an action
• authority — the right to give instructions

## Activity: Obedience song and results chart
You will need: Manila paper, Markers
1. In groups, list the results of disobedience on one side of a chart and the results of obedience on the other.
2. Present your chart to the class.
3. Sing a song on the benefits of obedience.
4. Each learner writes one thing he or she will obey promptly this week.

## Practice
1. Give three results of disobedience.
2. What happened to Adam and Eve after they disobeyed God?
3. Should you obey an adult who tells you to steal? Explain.

## Summary
• Disobedience brings danger, punishment, loss of trust and sin.
• Obedience brings blessing, safety and peace.
• Obey quickly and cheerfully, but never obey an instruction to do wrong.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: danger or injury; punishment; poor performance; loss of trust; quarrels; guilt; sin against God.
2. They felt ashamed, hid from God and were sent out of the Garden of Eden.
3. No. Obeying God comes first; say No and tell a trusted adult.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 4.3 OBEDIENCE
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which commandment says, "Respect your father and your mother"?
   A. Exodus 20:12
   B. Psalm 125:1
   C. Proverbs 12:19
   D. Matthew 6:9

2. What promise is given to those who honour their parents?
   A. They will become rich
   B. They will live a long time in the land
   C. They will never be sick
   D. They will never work

3. Which of these shows obedience to parents?
   A. Answering back rudely
   B. Coming home late
   C. Doing chores when asked
   D. Hiding from work

4. How does obeying parents and teachers help people live together?

5. Why should learners obey school rules?
   A. To please only the head teacher
   B. To keep order, safety and peace
   C. Because they have no choice
   D. To get gifts

6. Name two school rules.

7. Which is a result of disobedience?
   A. Trust
   B. Blessing
   C. Loss of trust
   D. Peace

8. What was the result of Adam and Eve's disobedience in Genesis 3?

9. Which is the best way to obey?
   A. Slowly and grumbling
   B. Quickly and cheerfully
   C. Only when watched
   D. Only when rewarded
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 4.3 OBEDIENCE
========================================

1. A. Exodus 20:12
   Exodus 20:12 is the commandment about honouring parents.

2. B. They will live a long time in the land
   Exodus 20:12 promises a long life in the land God gives.

3. C. Doing chores when asked
   Doing chores when asked is obeying parents.

4. It brings peace, fewer quarrels and good relationships at home and school.
   Obedience promotes harmonious co-existence.

5. B. To keep order, safety and peace
   Rules keep order, safety and peace for everyone.

6. Any two, for example arrive on time, wear correct uniform, keep the compound clean, do not fight.
   These are common school rules.

7. C. Loss of trust
   Disobedient children lose the trust of others.

8. They were ashamed, hid from God and were sent out of the Garden of Eden.
   Disobedience broke their close friendship with God.

9. B. Quickly and cheerfully
   True obedience is quick and cheerful.
